evidence: Read all 27 criteria (render 1, constraints 1, functional 16, polish 5, visual 4). No criterion enumerates requirements and then waives most of them: no 'need not', 'optional', 'at least one of', 'minor issues acceptable' or partial-credit escape anywhere in judge.toml, prompt.md or app_context.md (grep of the frozen tests/). Gates: render ends 'Assign 1 only if every check holds' (gates/render/judge.toml criterion authenticated_render); constraints' 'This gate does not grade roles, correctness, or feature completeness' (gates/constraints/judge.toml:35) disclaims things it never enumerated, it does not waive its own persistence/cross-browser steps, and its fail sentence matches them. Functional: multi-part criteria say 'Both parts must hold; failing either fails this criterion' and functional/prompt.md:26-28 states 'Every numbered leg and every sentence that names a step must hold ... A step you skipped ... fails the criterion', so each body is one conjunctive bar; the stated tolerances ('any clear format' for times, 'regardless of case', 'within about ten seconds', 'Any endpoint path ... acceptable' prompt.md:56) define a single bar rather than waiving enumerated items. Bundling a flow into one criterion is explicitly not a defect per SKILL.md known false positives and the workbook annotation. Polish is single-bar binaries (refusal_in_place's Fails line restates its body); visual likert anchors give one scale each. Every instance of residual wording looseness (Note, not a waiver): the trailing 'Fails if ...' summaries are narrower than their bodies in these places, so a judge that read them as exhaustive would have a laxer second reading: (1) signin_and_client_scope functional/judge.toml:44 requires Gwen's list to show 'Pryce lease dispute' and 'Pryce will' but :45 only fails if Gwen sees M-12; (2) wall_every_route :59 requires Dev's list to show M-11 and M-13 and :61 requires 'the thread and transcript answers are a plain not-available', but :63 fails only on M-12 data reaching Dev (a non-plain 403 'you are walled from this matter' answer is not named), unlike signin_and_client_scope :48 which does name the plain-refusal condition; (3) wall_added_live item 1 :83 requires M-13 to disappear from Sian's list, :88 fails only if she 'keeps seeing M-13 messages'; (4) deleted_and_expired_messages :112 and step 2 positive searches ('Clause 14 noted' / 'JUDGE-X1' found) are not in :116; (5) timer_changes :130 'the thread shows 7 days beside the title' and :131 'searching "executor" finds the held message' / transcript contains the executor message are not in :135; (6) search_and_transcript :239 positive 'notice received and filed finds the message' is not in :240. In every case the body sentence and the global rule at functional/prompt.md:26 both demand the stricter reading, and nothing tells the judge the Fails list is exhaustive, so there is one controlling full-credit bar; this is a consistency polish item, not a two-target defect. Adversarial tries: broken app that returns HTTP 403 'Walled from M-12 Fenwick' on replay - fails via :63 (title leaks) and :61; a 403 with no M-12 data but non-plain wording would still fail under :61 + prompt.md:26 though a careless judge might pass it on :63 alone (instance 2). Conforming alternative (e.g. 404 JSON {error:'not available'} or a different time format) - passes, no criterion forbids it. No configured judge run measured how the judge reads these summaries; this row is a textual check and does not require one.
suggested_fix: Optional: extend the 'Fails if' summaries to name the omitted legs (notably wall_every_route :63 'or if a thread/transcript replay is not a plain not-available'; timer_changes :135 'or if the 7-day setting is not shown beside the title'), or end each functional criterion with the template's 'Pass only if all legs hold.'
